edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Mammography does not change tumor biology, but it can shift some diagnoses earlier enough to prevent breast-cancer deaths at the cost of false positives and overdiagnosis.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 Hunger meta analysis in Rofo already points to mammography screening tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
